Bitcoin just crashed to a two-year low on a weekend — and if you own any, you felt it while the stock market was closed.

Bitcoin fell to a two-year low near $55,000 on Sunday before clawing back above $60,000 (Decrypt; market data, Nov. 22). It has now lost more than half its value since its October peak, and over $2 billion in leveraged bets were liquidated across the weekend, forcing even more selling.

Why it matters beyond traders: crypto now sits inside ETFs and retirement accounts, so a Sunday-night move lands in balances that used to only change on weekdays.

My take: an asset that trades 24/7 means your money can swing while you sleep on a Sunday — that round-the-clock volatility is the risk almost nobody prices in when they buy.

Do you hold any crypto, and did this weekend rattle you? 👇
